nodes.description: LHB encodes the beta subunit that gives LH its receptor specificity. Pathogenic variants are biallelic and of several classes: missense changes in the cystine knot (p.Gly36Asp, p.Cys46Arg), in-frame deletions (p.Lys40del, a four-leucine deletion in the signal peptide), splice-site variants in intron 2 (IVS2+1G>C, IVS2+1G>T), a nonsense variant (p.Trp28*) and a frameshift. All abolish production of bioactive LH, which is why the impact is recorded as loss of function regardless of the step affected.

nodes.description: Germ cell maturation fails for lack of intratesticular testosterone, giving azoospermia in most genotyped men until they are treated. The degree depends on residual LH activity: a man with a hypomorphic LHB allele whose LH kept low partial activity had complete, quantitatively normal spermatogenesis despite absent virilization, because a few mature Leydig cells made enough intratesticular testosterone. This is the pattern of the eponymous "fertile eunuch". In Lhb-null mice spermatogenesis stops at the round spermatid.

nodes.description: Without LH stimulation after birth, testicular Leydig cells stay undifferentiated and immature, testosterone synthesis is low, and the testes remain small. Prenatal male development is normal because placental hCG drives fetal Leydig cells through the same receptor. The Leydig cells keep their responsiveness to LH, which is why hCG restores testosterone production.
